chapter: Family background and the Tulsa music scene
title: His grandmother's language and 'Big Papa and Big Mamma'
summary: Describes his jet-black grandmother who said 'unnas' and the grandparents' nicknames.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So how I got my complexion -- my grandmother on the Simmons side was jet black, and she had a language of her own. Like, she's sit on the front porch in her rocking chair, she would quilt and make dresses and things like that. And rock all day long.

And she used to see a mile through her glasses, down on the end of her nose. And, like, she'd say, instead of saying 'my', 'I', she'd say 'unnas.' "Unnas children, unnas grandchildren." She'd say, "Unnas going to do this. Unnas going to do this," you know.
Do you know if that was some region -- (unintelligible)?
Not that I know of. She said unna.
And we all called her -- my grandfather and grandmother, Big Papa and Big Mamma. Because they were big. They were the heavies.
